Components / Surfaces

Rating input

.dr-rating · .dr-star · [data-on] · [aria-checked] · .dr-display--balance · .dr-center--tight · components/rating.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

How would you rate this order?

  1. 1.dr-display--balanceThe question, 22/700 with balanced line breaks. --tight puts it 8 above the stars rather than the column's 12, because a heading and the control it names are one group.
  2. 2.dr-ratingrole="radiogroup", five stars 8 apart, centred.
  3. 3.dr-star[aria-checked="true"]The value. It lands on one star: the star the user tapped.
  4. 4.dr-star[data-on]The fill, which runs up to the value. --color-rating #E4A11B is 2.05:1 on the page, so it never carries the state alone. The radio state does.
  5. 5.dr-star:not([data-on])An empty star: --color-rating-empty, grey, with no outline.
  6. 6.dr-icThe star glyph, 32 inside a 44 target (HIG · 44pt). It is the one glyph in the system that fills instead of stroking, because a rating is a quantity, not an icon.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: (.dr-rating, .dr-star).

States

Light

Try it: hover, press, Tab. Follows the theme switch above.

The five stars as rate builds them, the fourth checked.

When to use

The rating input stands on one screen, rate, in 3 files: rate, rate-aerial and rate-inspection. It is the only place in the product where a score is given rather than reported. It is an input: five real buttons in a radio group, each a 44pt target with an accessible name. The radio group replaced five aria-pressed toggles, which described one rating as five independent switches (WCAG 4.1.2).

A score that is only read, such as an operator's 4.9 on a card, must not be a row of buttons announcing a state it cannot change. That is the earned score, which writes the value as a number and puts no stops in the tab order. On rate the pair of question and stars sits 8 apart, and .dr-main--zones puts 24 around the pair (see screen layout).

The question names the order, not the drone: How would you rate this order? The stars are named 1 star to 5 stars. Under them comes an optional review field. The action bar holds Submit review, the screen's one green control, on top, and Book again, a secondary, under it.

Sources: DESIGN.md § The earned score (Why not .dr-rating) · § Neutral (rating colour) · components/rating.css · microcopy.md § rate · ui/kit.html § Rating input

Rule and anti-rule

Do

How would you rate this order?

Submit review Book again

The client gives a score after the order is complete: a question, five stars, and Submit review as the commit, over Book again. This is rate, with the review field between them left out.

Don’t

An operator's score shown to a client as five tappable buttons. A score the reader cannot change is not an input. It would put five stops in the tab order and announce a choice that does not exist (WCAG 4.1.2). Use the earned score.
